questions.q: Which of the following ketones gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent?
questions.explain: Fructose is an α-hydroxy ketone; the alkaline reagent converts it through an enediol into an aldehyde, which is then oxidised. Simple ketones resist this mild oxidation.

questions.q: Which pair of compounds can be distinguished by Tollens' test?
questions.explain: Propanal is oxidised and gives a silver mirror while propanone does not react. In every other pair both compounds reduce Tollens' reagent (aromatic aldehydes, ketoses and formic acid all respond).

questions.q: Hex-4-enal is warmed with Tollens' reagent and the mixture is then acidified. The organic product is:
questions.explain: Tollens' reagent oxidises only the –CHO group, leaving the C=C intact; acidification converts the carboxylate to the free acid. A strong oxidant such as KMnO₄ would also attack the double bond.

questions.q: But-1-yne is added to Tollens' reagent. What is observed?
options: A silver mirror, because the alkyne is oxidised to a carboxylate
No change, because alkynes have no C=O group
A white precipitate of silver acetylide, because the ≡C–H hydrogen is acidic
questions.explain: A terminal alkyne replaces its acidic ≡C–H hydrogen by silver to give R–C≡C–Ag. This is not an oxidation, so no mirror forms.
